English construction: Restrictive relative clause
Example: “The cups that have blue handles belong on this shelf.”
The relative clause identifies which cups are meant.

English construction: Supplementary relative clause
Example: “My only bicycle, which has a bent wheel, is in the shed.”
The commas mark extra information about an already identified bicycle.

text:
English construction: Relative clause with an omitted object pronoun
Example: “The book I borrowed is on your desk.”
The object relative pronoun can be omitted; the clause is equivalent to 'that I borrowed'.

English construction: Possessive relative clause
Example: “The musician whose violin was missing waited by the door.”
Whose marks the relationship between the musician and the violin.

English construction: Free relative clause
Example: “Take whatever you need.”
Whatever you need functions as a noun phrase without a separate antecedent.
